_doc: fc-system2-005 (system, run_shell_command with command reasoning): the user wants the 3 largest files in /var/log/ by size, in human-readable form. The model has to construct the right command — many variants work (ls -lhS | head -3, du -h | sort -hr | head -3, find ... | head -3, etc.). command_equivalents whitelists the common variants — including header-skipping forms, since a bare `ls -l`-based pipeline emits a 'total NNN' header line that `head -3` counts against the 3-file budget (review of PR #34, N1). The naive `| head -3` spelling is kept in the list too: the case tests command-construction reasoning, not shell perfection. The reasoning required: shell-construction skill. Single tool exposed.
prompt: Find the 3 largest files in /var/log/ by size. Use a single run_shell_command call that lists them in descending size order with their sizes in human-readable form.
system: Before answering, write your reasoning inside a <thought>...</thought> block. Then call the tool using the <tool_call> format.

function.name: run_shell_command
function.description: Execute a shell command in a sandboxed non-interactive shell and return its combined stdout+stderr. Read-only commands are recommended; commands that modify the filesystem require explicit confirmation via `confirm: true`.

confirm.description: Must be true for any command that writes outside /tmp or invokes package managers.
